spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 587.5618 nm (the d line, the wavelength the source's Nd refers to), converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact, at 20 C and 101325 Pa)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states indices at the d line only. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; the single d-line index pair does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.conditions: the publication's parameter lines above TABLE 11 state f = 1.30-1.88 mm; 1.30 mm is the short focal length extremity, the state this record transcribes
effective_focal_length_mm.note: stated to two decimal places, so the publication's own rounding interval is +/-0.005 mm

back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point
back_focal_length_mm.conditions: the publication's parameter lines state fB = 0.05-0.05 mm, i.e. 0.05 mm at both extremities; the table's last thickness, from surface 12 to the image, is the same 0.05 mm

total_track_mm.note: sum of the publication's stated thicknesses from surface 1 to the image plane at the wide end; it equals the importer's image plane position

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length
comparison.why: the rule presupposes a source value stated to about five significant figures. This publication states the focal length to two decimals (1.30 mm) and the back focus to one (0.05 mm), so the stated values are design targets, not measurements. Against the effective focal length the engine is 0.001261 mm high, which fails the rule (tolerance 1.40e-4 mm, 9.0x over) but lies inside the publication's own rounding interval of 1.30 +/- 0.005 mm. Against the back focal length the two numbers are not the same quantity: the publication's 0.05 mm is the image distance at the stated 10 mm object distance, while the engine's -0.112408 mm is the infinite-conjugate rear focal distance that the paraxial command reports

f_number.definition: the F-number the publication states in its parameter lines (FE = 5.7-7.2); 5.7 is the short focal length extremity, the state this record transcribes. The publication does not say which F-number convention FE is

aperture.note: the stop opening in the Project (0.2523 mm) was derived from this stated F-number, not stated by the source; see the SEMI_DIAMETER_DERIVED approximation

field.definition: the publication's parameter lines state W = 70.4-36.2, read as the full angle of field (2 omega) at the short and long focal length extremities respectively
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED (parameter lines: W = 70.4-36.2); the half field is DERIVED as half of the stated full field
field.convention_note: the publication calls W the angle of field and states one value per zoom state, which is the conventional full field. Read that way, an image height of f*tan(35.2 deg) = 0.918 mm is consistent with the stated magnification of -0.12 at a 10 mm object distance, which implies 0.846 mm; the two differ by about 8 %, consistent with a distortion the prescription does not state. The two statements are therefore mutually consistent, and this record does not assert an image height

materials.policy: Every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd. A patent table gives nd and vd only, which cannot define a dispersion curve; fitting one would invent a material. Published catalog glasses were compared as a cross-check and are recorded under catalog_comparisons, never substituted.

catalog_comparisons.basis: cross-check only: the closest published glass by index; it is compared, never substituted, and the Project keeps the source's own nd
no published catalog glass in the 1226-glass index lies within |dnd| <= 5e-5 and |dvd| <= 0.05 of this pair; the nearest is listed and is not close enough to be a comparison

approximations.detail: the publication states this prescription in two states. Its parameter lines give f = 1.30-1.88 mm, FE = 5.7-7.2, W = 70.4-36.2, ODIS = -10 / -2.5, m = -0.12 / -0.66 and the two variable spacings, surface 4 at 1.09-0.40 mm and surface 9 at 0.93-2.90 mm. This record transcribes the short focal length extremity (wide end), because the publication lists it first in every parameter line, it is the overview state, and its object distance of 10 mm is the one the description's normal-viewing use implies. The long extremity is not represented in the Project; it was built once as a scratch cross-check and its values are recorded under first_order.cross_checks
every glass is a constant index at the source's stated nd; the source's vd is recorded but no dispersion curve is modelled, so axial colour and chromatic focal shift are not represented
the Project is evaluated at the d line only

the source states no clear apertures. The stop opening was derived from the stated F-number: a paraxial marginal-ray trace with a 0.2523 mm opening at the diaphragm gives an image-space F-number of 5.70 at the wide end, the stated FE. Each surface's clear semi-diameter is the axial marginal-ray height there plus a margin, growing toward the image side (0.70 mm at surfaces 1-4, 0.75 at 5-6, 0.80 at 7, 0.85 at 8, 0.90 at 9-12), and is capped so that every element keeps a positive edge thickness, which the source's own radii allow up to 0.77 mm at surface 2. Semi-diameters set the stop plate and the solid checks only; they do not enter the first-order values

the surface table marks surface 9 as aspherical, but the publication's aspherical-coefficient table for this table names surface 4 (K = 0.00, A4 = 0.10542e-1, A6 = -0.18897e-2, A8 = 0), which contradicts the surface table, and the coefficient cells are broken across rows by the x10^-n formatting. Assigning those coefficients to surface 9 would be a guess, so the Project keeps surface 9's vertex radius (r = -2.782 mm) as a sphere. First-order values are unchanged by this; the record makes no claim about the aberration correction the asphere provides
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled
the two cemented interfaces (source surfaces 8 and 11) are modelled as a shared surface between the two glasses; no cement thickness is stated and none is added

unsupported_constructs.construct: the aspherical deformation of surface 9 (A4, A6)
unsupported_constructs.detail: the source marks surface 9 aspherical but its coefficient table names surface 4; the coefficients are therefore not represented (see the ASPHERIC_TERMS_NOT_MODELLED approximation). The surface is modelled at its vertex radius, so the first-order prescription is complete and the aberration correction is not claimed

conversion.counts_note: the importer's 'elements' counts glass members; the source table's 12 surfaces form 7 glass elements, of which 2 are cemented pairs, grouped into 5 members plus the diaphragm

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0
project solids reported no error-severity finding and the importer raised no warning

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED, and not DIFFERS: the publication does state an EFL (1.30 mm) and a back focus (0.05 mm) in millimetres, but to two and one significant figures respectively, so the format's 1e-5 + 1e-4*scale rule cannot be applied to them. The engine's EFL is 1.301261 mm, which is 0.001261 mm high, 9.0x the tolerance but inside the publication's own rounding interval of 1.30 +/- 0.005 mm; the engine's paraxial BFL is the infinite-conjugate rear focal distance (-0.112408 mm), a different quantity from the publication's finite-conjugate 0.05 mm
the finite-conjugate back focus is reproduced: the stated 10 mm object images at z = 8.43541 mm by the engine's cardinal points, against the design's image plane at 8.44 mm

the transcription of both states is verified independently: the stop opening, derived once from the stated 5.7 at the wide end, gives 7.108 at the long extremity against the stated 7.2, and the engine's long-extremity EFL is 1.884853 mm against the stated 1.88 mm
the object distance is the source's stated 10 mm for the wide end (ODIS = -10), not infinity, so the Project is built for that finite conjugate
surface 9 is aspherical in the source; its coefficients are not modelled (see unsupported_constructs). First-order values are unaffected
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted
